doi 10.1167/iovs.10-5598 = PMID 20881303; abstract sentence verbatim (full text paywalled). Yorio 2020 (Expert Rev Ophthalmol 15(3):145-157, PMID 38274668, PMC10810227) verified verbatim: 'Although not as effective as DEX in inducing OHT, mapracorat still increased IOP compared to vehicle treated rabbits'. Untested stands; add NCT00905450 IOP AE row (see missing).

missing: Safety judgement omits NCT00905450 (Phase 2 post-cataract, results posted 2020-09-03), whose >=5% AE table DOES list 'Intraocular pressure increased': 1% BID 2/60, 2% QD 0/28, 2% BID 0/28, 2% QID 2/60, 3% QD 0/59, 3% BID 1/60, 3% QID 1/60 vs vehicle 3/60. Pooled mapracorat 6/355 (1.7%) vs vehicle 5%. Still untested (18-day window, AE term not measured IOP, no steroid arm), but the draft's 'no trial posted an IOP term' framing should cite it. https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00905450

The rabbit IOP prediction is characterised as a REDUCED rise, not no rise, by three independent readers, which strengthens the draft's 'contested' point: Shafiee's own conclusion says 'reduced effects in IOP'; Baiula & Spampinato 2014 (doi 10.2174/1871528113666141106101356, PMID 25373600): 'mapracorat induces a lower increase of intraocular pressure in comparison to the classical glucocorticoid dexamethasone'; Baiula 2014 (doi 10.2147/DDDT.S62659): 'displays a reduced ability to increase intraocular pressure'. The testable prediction is therefore relative to dexamethasone, and no mapracorat trial ran a steroid arm, so neither Phase 3 AE silence at a 5% threshold nor the Phase 2 row can score same or contra.

If the cross-trial loteprednol argument is retained anywhere, the co-primary pain endpoint should be shown alongside AC cells: Phase 3 pain-free day 8 = 130/207 (63%), 165/245 (67%), 172/240 (72%) vs vehicle 55/52/49%; loteprednol gel label 73-76% vs 42-46%. Also sub-loteprednol, but a smaller gap than the AC-cell endpoint.

The post-cataract Phase 3 trio + rabbit paracentesis (Shafiee 2011) + Valeant 10-K is a coherent magnitude-miss story for a DIFFERENT context (postoperative ocular inflammation x SEGRA). If the atlas carries that context, contra belongs there, not here.
CAC co-primary conjunctival redness (investigator-scored) also sits below vehicle in all six arms (1.56-2.05 vs 2.14), supporting the direction-only reading; worth quoting next to itching.
rule_questions: Does a registry outcome table with NO posted statistics and NO comparator arm count as a 'published comparison' sufficient for same/contra (via comparison_stated=false), or only for untested? The brief allows self-juxtaposition but is silent on whether the patient side must carry a test. If statistics are required, efficacy 2020 falls to untested rather than same.

When the model's prediction is a magnitude claim (steroid-equivalence) and the context's only patient trial never ran a steroid arm, is the direction-only agreement scored same, or is the magnitude claim scored untested? Here the two readings coexist; the draft chose contra on an out-of-context magnitude argument.

Can out-of-context evidence carry a status in this context: post-cataract Phase 3 vs the rabbit paracentesis model, and a cross-trial comparison with a different steroid's label (loteprednol, not dexamethasone)? If yes, the draft's contra is defensible; if no, same (or untested).
Is an uncited field convention (the >=1-unit CAC itching bar) admissible as the yardstick for a magnitude miss? It is not a source under rule 1.

Valeant FY2013 10-K (accession 0000885590-14-000025, filed 2014-02-28) exists and reads verbatim: 'wrote-off (i) an IPR&D asset of $14.4 million related to the termination of the Mapracorat development program ... resulting from analysis of Phase 3 study results'. It is not a rule-1 source type, concerns the post-cataract Phase 3s, and states no model-vs-patient comparison, so under the brief it changes nothing; the draft correctly keeps it in judgement only. Should the brief say whether sponsor filings may feed source_calls_it?
Can AE tables posted at a >=5% threshold over 14-18 days ever score a safety cell when the model's prediction is relative to a steroid comparator that was never run? Here: no.
